articles.title: Viral Audio of Meerut CO Triggers Row Over Videography Inside Police Station
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A fresh controversy has erupted in Meerut after a 29-second audio clip of Brahmapuri Circle Officer Soumya Asthana surfaced on social media.

body.html:
A fresh controversy has erupted in Meerut after a 29-second audio clip of Brahmapuri Circle Officer Soumya Asthana surfaced on social media. In the clip, she is allegedly heard directing subordinates to immediately register a case if a journalist engages in videography inside a police station.

The viral audio has sparked widespread discussion, prompting a clarification from Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Avinash Pandey. The SSP stated that the directive was not aimed at accredited journalists but at certain “portal owners” who were allegedly recording unnecessary videos inside the premises. He clarified that there is no blanket restriction on the media.

The issue reportedly pertains to an incident at the TP Nagar Police Station. Attempts to contact CO Soumya Asthana for her response were unsuccessful.

From a legal standpoint, media videography inside a police station is generally not treated as a violation under the Official Secrets Act. Courts have clarified that a police station does not qualify as a “prohibited place” under Section 2(8) of the Act. However, recording must not obstruct official duties or interfere with ongoing investigations.

In an official statement, Meerut Police said the viral audio clip was partial and did not reflect the full context. According to police, the matter involved an unrecognized portal operator who was recording a private conversation between two parties inside the station. The Circle Officer had reportedly issued guidelines to ensure compliance with the Uttar Pradesh Police Social Media Policy 2023.

Police officials have said efforts are underway to clear any confusion arising from the viral clip, while discussions on the limits of media access inside police premises continue.

articles.title: SHOCKING: Daughter-in-law Slaps Mother-in-law 3 Times in 30 Seconds | Gonda CCTV Viral
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A disturbing incident has surfaced from the Nawabganj police station area of Gonda, Uttar Pradesh, where a daughter-in-law allegedly slapped her mother-in-law three times within 30 seconds following an argument.

body.html:
A disturbing incident has surfaced from the Nawabganj police station area of Gonda, Uttar Pradesh, where a daughter-in-law allegedly slapped her mother-in-law three times within 30 seconds following an argument. The entire episode was reportedly captured on CCTV cameras installed inside the house.

According to police sources, the complainant, Sarita, a resident of Rewa village under Nawabganj police station limits in Gonda, alleged that her son Brijesh Maurya, a loco pilot posted in Kanpur, had a love marriage with Anita Maurya on February 14, 2025.

Sarita claimed that since the marriage, Anita had been frequently harassing and assaulting her. On February 28, an argument reportedly broke out between the two, during which Anita allegedly slapped the 50-year-old woman three times in quick succession. The CCTV footage, now circulating on social media, purportedly shows Anita holding Sarita’s hand while she was seated on a sofa and assaulting her.

At the time of the incident, Brijesh was reportedly on duty in Kanpur.

Sarita has lodged a formal complaint at the Nawabganj police station and submitted the CCTV footage as evidence. Police have initiated an investigation into the matter.

Reports indicate that Anita has been missing from the house since the incident. Authorities have stated that appropriate action will be taken based on the findings of the inquiry.

articles.title: Azamgarh Shock: Speeding Car Smashes Into House Boundary, Driver Held After Chaos
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: In Uttar Pradesh’s Azamgarh, an out-of-control car rammed into the boundary wall of a roadside house in Badarka under Kotwali police station limits. The shocking incident was caught on CCTV. Locals gathered at the spot and allegedly thrashed the driver before police intervened.

body.html:
In Uttar Pradesh’s Azamgarh, an out-of-control car rammed into the boundary wall of a roadside house in Badarka under Kotwali police station limits. The shocking incident was caught on CCTV.

Locals gathered at the spot and allegedly thrashed the driver before police intervened. Two people have been arrested. The matter was later settled with compensation.

Reports suggest the driver was under the influence of bhang. Residents say had the impact been slightly stronger, the house could have collapsed.

Azamgarh Police stated that the matter was taken into immediate cognisance and necessary action is being carried out by the Kotwali SHO.

articles.title: ‘No MLA Will Save You’: Audio of Heated Call Between Ex-MLA Gorakhnath Baba and SDM Surfaces
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A purported audio clip of a heated phone conversation between former Milkipur MLA Gorakhnath Baba and Milkipur SDM Sudhir Kumar has surfaced in Ayodhya, triggering political and administrative controversy.

body.html:
A purported audio clip of a heated phone conversation between former Milkipur MLA Gorakhnath Baba and Milkipur SDM Sudhir Kumar has surfaced in Ayodhya, triggering political and administrative controversy.

In the recording, Gorakhnath Baba is heard warning the SDM, saying, “You don’t know our horoscope properly. If Gorakhnath Baba gets angry, no government MLA will be able to save you.” The exchange allegedly took place over a dispute related to construction of an Anganwadi centre in Sumerpur (Pura) village under the Amaniganj development block.

Dispute Over Anganwadi Construction
According to local sources, on Saturday night a youth allegedly began construction on land earmarked for an Anganwadi centre. The Gram Sabha had earlier passed a proposal on March 6, 2025, to construct an Anganwadi centre and RRC on plot number 1189G. Funds amounting to ₹2.5 lakh were reportedly sanctioned for the project.

However, villagers had earlier opposed the construction and allegedly demolished the structure. Despite complaints and repeated representations to the administration, the work did not resume. The matter was subsequently taken to the Lucknow Bench of the Allahabad High Court, which reportedly issued an order permitting the Gram Panchayat to proceed with construction.

Despite the court’s direction, fresh construction allegedly began on the same plot by another individual, prompting renewed tension.

What the Audio Reveals
In the viral clip, Gorakhnath Baba accuses the SDM of ignoring repeated requests to begin construction despite legal sanction and court approval. He alleges administrative inaction, hints at political pressure, and warns of consequences in the 2027 elections.

At one point, he is heard saying that if he comes to the SDM’s office, “who has the authority to confront us?” He also refers to alleged cases being filed against supporters and claims harassment of party workers.

SDM Sudhir Kumar is heard attempting to calm the situation, assuring that he had spoken to the village pradhan and that work would begin.

Administrative Intervention
After the matter came to light, the District Magistrate intervened and ordered the immediate halt of the disputed construction. An administrative team visited the site and assessed the situation, following which all construction activity was stopped.

Village head Adarsh Srivastava stated that despite repeated meetings with officials, including the SDM and former MLA, no progress had been made on the sanctioned project, forcing them to approach the High Court.

Political Undercurrents
The issue has also drawn attention due to the alleged involvement of current MLA Chandrabhanu Paswan, intensifying speculation about factionalism within the Bharatiya Janata Party.

Authorities have not yet issued an official statement regarding the authenticity of the audio clip. The situation remains under administrative review.

articles.title: Drunk Student Held After Mercedes Crash, Attempt to Run Over Constable in Gachibowli
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A 24-year-old student was arrested on Sunday after allegedly crashing his luxury car into another vehicle and later attempting to flee by accelerating towards a traffic constable in Gachibowli while under the influence of alcohol.

body.html:
A 24-year-old student was arrested on Sunday after allegedly crashing his luxury car into another vehicle and later attempting to flee by accelerating towards a traffic constable in Gachibowli while under the influence of alcohol.

The accused, Gurrampati Tarun, a resident of Narsingi, was taken into custody by the Gachibowli Police in connection with two separate cases. The white Mercedes-Benz car (TS 07 EX 5556) involved in the incident has been seized, and the accused was produced before a magistrate.

According to police, the first complaint was filed around 12.30 p.m. by Rahul Kamaraju, who stated that he was driving from Narsingi towards Kukatpally when the Mercedes allegedly rammed his vehicle from behind at Nanakramguda. The impact caused his car to lose control and crash into a footpath divider, resulting in damage. The accused then fled towards the Outer Ring Road in Gachibowli. A traffic Home Guard alerted the control room through a wireless message, leading to registration of a case.

In a second complaint lodged around 2 p.m., traffic constable E. Narsimhulu of Gachibowli Traffic Police stated that he was on duty at the IIIT Junction when he received instructions via wireless to intercept the same vehicle involved in the earlier accident.

At about 10.50 a.m., upon spotting the car, he signalled it to stop. Though the vehicle initially slowed down, it allegedly accelerated suddenly towards the constable, causing him to fall onto the bonnet. Police said the driver continued driving in a rash and negligent manner despite knowing the constable was on the bonnet, thereby endangering his life. The vehicle was eventually stopped after other motorists intervened and blocked its path.

CCTV footage reportedly shows the accused driving recklessly while the constable was on the bonnet. A breath analyser test conducted later revealed a blood alcohol concentration of 160 mg per 100 ml, far exceeding the permissible limit under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

Further investigation is in progress.

articles.title: Hathras: Why Rashtriya Savarna Parishad is performing Pind Daan for PM Modi?
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Pankaj Dhawaraiya of Rashtriya Savarna Parishad performed a symbolic Pind Daan of PM Narendra Modi in Hathras. Staging a sit-in at Kanchan Nagar for 23 days, the protest targets the proposed UGC Bill and non-compliance with Supreme Court orders on the SC/ST Act.

body.html:
Pankaj Dhawaraiya of Rashtriya Savarna Parishad performed a symbolic Pind Daan of PM Narendra Modi in Hathras. Staging a sit-in at Kanchan Nagar for 23 days, the protest targets the proposed UGC Bill and non-compliance with Supreme Court orders on the SC/ST Act. Intelligence agencies are currently on high alert in Uttar Pradesh as the 'anti-Sanatan' and 'anti-upper caste' allegations spark local debate.

* * *

In Hathras, Uttar Pradesh, a controversial protest unfolded as Pankaj Dhawaraiya, president of the Rashtriya Savarna Parishad, performed a symbolic “Pind Daan” ritual in front of a photograph of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Dhawaraiya, who identifies himself as a leader representing the upper-caste community, said the act was carried out in protest against the proposed UGC Bill and alleged non-compliance with Supreme Court directives concerning the SC/ST Act. He claimed that his padyatra had been stopped by the administration 23 days ago, following which he has been staging a sit-in protest at Kanchan Nagar.

On the 23rd day of the agitation, Dhawaraiya and other Parishad office-bearers gathered at the protest site and performed the ritual, raising slogans against the Prime Minister. He alleged that the Prime Minister’s policies were “anti-upper caste” and “anti-Sanatan,” and stated that the protest would continue.

Intelligence agencies are reportedly monitoring activities at the protest site amid heightened political sensitivities.

The incident has sparked debate locally, though no immediate administrative action has been reported.

articles.title: UKG Girl Crushed by School Bus in Aligarh After Floor Breaks; Driver Flees, Villagers Block Road
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: An eight-year-old UKG student was crushed to death after falling through a broken metal sheet on the floor of a moving school bus in the Dholna area near Aligarh–Kasganj border on Saturday afternoon.

body.html:
An eight-year-old UKG student was crushed to death after falling through a broken metal sheet on the floor of a moving school bus in the Dholna area near Aligarh–Kasganj border on Saturday afternoon.

The deceased, Ananya, a resident of Nay Bhai village under Dadon police station limits in Aligarh, was returning home from Mount International School in Budhiya Kaser along with her elder brother.

According to reports, the incident occurred around 3 pm near Nagla Sadhu/Birhara village in the Dholna area of Kasganj. The bus had first dropped children in Dholna and was heading towards Gangiri when a portion of the floor beneath Ananya’s seat, located above the rear wheel, suddenly gave way. She fell directly onto the road and was run over by the same bus.

Her brother, who was travelling with her, raised an alarm, shouting at the driver to stop the bus. The driver halted the vehicle, lifted the injured child and allegedly threatened the brother not to inform anyone about the incident.

The driver then reportedly informed the girl’s father about her “injury” and drove towards Malasai intersection. By the time she was brought there, Ananya had succumbed to her injuries.

Villagers who witnessed the bus fleeing chased it for nearly two kilometres and intercepted it at Malasai intersection. The driver was caught and allegedly beaten by an angry crowd. The bus was also vandalised, and locals blocked the Aligarh–Kasganj road in protest.

On receiving information, police from Gangiri, Chharra and Dadon stations reached the spot and pacified the crowd after nearly an hour. The body was sent to Kasganj for postmortem, as the accident occurred within Dholna police station limits.

CO Chharra Sanjeev Tomar said the bus floor was broken at the seat where the girl had been sitting, leading to her fall under the wheel. He admitted that the vehicle appeared to be in poor condition and further investigation would determine whether it was operating without valid fitness certification. A checking drive against unsafe school buses has been announced.

The girl’s father, Ravi Kumar, who runs a public service centre at Gangiri intersection, has lodged a complaint against the school management. Police said legal action will proceed based on the complaint and postmortem report.

The tragic incident has left the family devastated ahead of Holi celebrations, with relatives and villagers demanding strict action against those responsible.

articles.title: Truck Drags Tata Nexon for 1.5 KM on Dabra–Gwalior Highway; Terrifying Video Goes Viral
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A speeding truck was seen dragging a car for nearly 1.5 kilometres after ramming into it on the Dabra–Gwalior highway on Sunday morning. Fortunately, no casualties were reported. The incident took place near Bajhera village, outside the Tekanpur limits.

body.html:
A speeding truck was seen dragging a car for nearly 1.5 kilometres after ramming into it on the Dabra–Gwalior highway on Sunday morning. Fortunately, no casualties were reported.

The incident took place near Bajhera village, outside the Tekanpur limits. According to sources, truck number RJ 11 GC 2456 collided with a Tata Nexon (MP07-ZG-9779). Following the impact, the car became lodged in the front portion of the truck.

Instead of stopping, the truck driver allegedly continued driving, dragging the car up to the area near Defence Park. The entire episode was captured on video and has since gone viral on social media.

Three persons were travelling in the car, including an officer of the Special Armed Force (SAF). They were reportedly returning from Orchha. Despite the shocking nature of the incident, all occupants escaped without serious injuries.

Eyewitnesses said the car occupants kept shouting and banging on the truck, urging the driver to stop, but he did not respond. A local resident, Sebu Gurjar, chased the truck on his motorcycle and repeatedly signalled the driver to halt. Other passersby also attempted to stop the vehicle.

After dragging the car for around 1.5 kilometres, the driver allegedly pushed it towards a roadside ditch and attempted to flee. However, locals intercepted the truck in the Bilaua area. The driver was reportedly assaulted by angry bystanders before police arrived at the scene.

Station House Officer Geetesh Sharma of Antri Police Station said that no formal complaint has been received so far. “If someone lodges a complaint, a case will be registered,” he said. The truck has been seized for further investigation.

articles.title: Delivery Boy Assaulted in Greater Noida West Housing Society; Residents Demand Eviction of Foreign
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A Nigerian national allegedly assaulted a delivery boy at Samriddhi Grand Avenue Housing Society in the Bisrakh police station area of Greater Noida West following a dispute over payment.

body.html:
A Nigerian national allegedly assaulted a delivery boy at Samriddhi Grand Avenue Housing Society in the Bisrakh police station area of Greater Noida West following a dispute over payment.

According to reports, the accused, identified as Ismail Manzoor, had ordered goods online late in the evening. When the delivery executive sought payment, an argument reportedly broke out, after which the accused allegedly assaulted him. Residents who intervened were also allegedly abused, leading to tension within the society premises.

Following the incident, residents staged a protest and informed the Bisrakh Police Station. A video of the protest has surfaced on social media, showing residents confronting the accused, while some other foreign nationals accompanying him were seen attempting to pacify the situation.

Residents alleged that the tenant had been living in the society for nearly a year and had been involved in previous incidents of misconduct. They further claimed that the flat owner had rented the apartment without informing the society’s maintenance team. Some residents also alleged that the tenant initially obtained the flat under the pretext of being a cancer patient and later moved in with family members. Complaints were also raised regarding smoking in public areas in violation of society rules.

Bisrakh police station in-charge Krishna Gopal Sharma said that police reached the spot after receiving information and brought the situation under control. He stated that the foreign national had arrived in India on a medical visa and had rented a doctor’s flat. The dispute reportedly arose over payment for the delivery.

Police said they have spoken to the flat owner and directed him to ensure the tenant vacates the premises. Further inquiry into the matter is underway.
